messages:
alex: Heads up — saw two OOMs on prod inference nodes last night that look tied to KV cache growth after the kernel-selection + the new batching heuristic rollout. Repro logs and pprof attached, digging in now.

maya: Can you paste the log snippets or a link? How bad is the blip (latency/failed requests)?

alex: Errors were `OOM` during token gen, ~120 failed requests over 15m on two hosts. From pprof heap diff: 

```
kv_cache_bytes: 12.1GB -> 19.3GB (14k allocations)
alloc_site: runtime.kv.append -> runtime.kv.retain -> kernel_select.large_kv_path
hot stacks (sampled):
  34.2%  kernel_select.large_kv_path
  22.1%  batcher.continuous_batcher.append
  10.7%  kv_cache.stitch_if_possible
```

So looks like continuous batching + large-kernel path increased reuse window and prevented timely compaction -> slab fragmentation + growth.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-54 created and page sent to #eng-oncall.

sergio: Yep — suspected interaction. The new batching heuristic tries to merge short contexts into a shared continuous batch, which extends the KV lifetime per-request. Coupled with the kernel selection change that prefers the `large_kv_path` (skips micro-compaction to favor throughput), we missed the compaction signals. Net effect: reuse increases, but we accumulate many small freed segments -> fragmentation and eventual OOM.

taylor: Short-term mitigation options: flip kernel selection to prefer `compact_friendly` on the two affected pools, and reduce continuous-batch window from 200ms -> 80ms. Canary on 2 nodes first. That should reduce reuse window and force earlier compaction.

alex: Agree. Also propose a soft-evict path: when `kv_pool_headroom < threshold` trigger per-session prefix-throttle + async `kv_compact_now()` and an immediate fallback to `small_kv_kernel` for new requests.

maya: I can push the config flip to canary cluster. Command I'll run:

```
# canary config flip (k8s configmap)
kubectl -n inference patch configmap runtime-config --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/batching/window_ms","value":80},{"op":"replace","path":"/kernel/preference","value":"compact_friendly"}]'
```

I'll also add a Grafana panel for `kv_pool_headroom`, `kv_frag_ratio`, `per_session_kv_growth` p99 so we can watch during the canary.

sergio: I'll add a lightweight safety backoff in the runtime: pseudo-config below. If growth rate > 50MB/s for session -> apply prefix-throttle and schedule background compaction.

```
if session.kv_growth_rate > 50MB/s:
  session.apply_prefix_throttle(0.5)  # halve append rate
  runtime.schedule_background("kv_compact", session.id)
  kernel_selector.force_kernel("small_kv_kernel")
```

ritz: We saw something similar last year but the threshold was too high (1GB). Fragmentation spikes once reuse window > ~1e6 tokens. Suggest conservative session cap: max_session_kv_tokens = 512k while we iterate. Also add eviction score to prioritize compactable slabs.

alex: Action items:
- maya: push canary + dashboard (ETA 30m)
- sergio: implement safety backoff + background compaction task (PR by EOD)
- taylor: prep rollback runbook & keep standby capacity (2 spare nodes)
- alex: draft incident summary and follow-up evals (perf regression tests to catch this interplay)

Also: add unit/integration test to simulate continuous batching + kernel selection combos to detect growth patterns early.

maya: starting canary now. tagging @sergio @taylor, will report metrics in 15m.

sergio: quick note — when you flip kernel pref, ensure feature-flag TTL 1h so we can auto-revert if headroom doesn't stabilize.

alex: Great. If canary looks good we'll roll to prod with throttled ramp. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
